reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key premises. The claims about specific precipitate types, volume fractions, their effect on Cr2O3 scale continuity, short-circuit diffusion, and failure mechanisms are entirely unsupported by referenced prior work.
premises: Aging at 750°C/50h produces ~25-30 vol% L12 and Cr/Fe-depleted L21 precipitates at cell walls
Cr-depleted precipitates delay formation of a continuous protective Cr2O3 scale
Precipitate–matrix interfaces act as short-circuit diffusion paths for oxygen ingress
Delayed Cr2O3 scale leads to a thicker, less coherent duplex-to-trilayer oxide with inner Al/Ti-rich region
Multi-layered oxide scale causes microcracking and spallation, enabling catastrophic failure
